[CORRECTION after gate feedback] Coordinator caught a flaky new test: DetailSubform.test.tsx 'the draft re-syncs...after a save conflict' failed ~1/3 runs (683 passed/3 failed/683/1 failed observed). Root cause found (NOT a timeout issue, NOT papered over): MonthAmountInput's/MonthCell's useEffect(()=>setDraft(String(value)),[value]) unconditionally fires once on MOUNT too (redundant no-op, useState initializer already set draft correctly). Because these components mount as a side effect of an ASYNC fetch (row only exists after fetchDetailLines/fetchTrips resolves + setRows/setCards, outside the test render()'s act() scope), React can defer flushing that pending mount effect past when waitFor resolves. If it flushes in the SAME act() batch as a user's onChange, it's a last-write race: the stale mount effect's setDraft(oldValue) can win and clobber what was just typed. Confirmed empirically via temporary console.error instrumentation: on a failing run, trace showed 'onChange fired -> effect fired, setting draft to 100' (the OLD value) AFTER the keystroke. Fix: frontend/src/subform/MonthAmountInput.tsx + frontend/src/grid/MonthCell.tsx both now use a useRef(lastSyncedValue) guard so the effect only calls setDraft when value actually changed since last sync -- mount becomes a true no-op (nothing to race), external changes (save/refetch) still resync deterministically. Applied to BOTH components for consistency since MonthCell has the identical latent pattern (its own tests never caught it because MonthCell always mounts synchronously there). Verified: previously-flaky test run 20/20 in isolation post-fix (was ~40-50% fail rate before); TripManager decimal/resync tests run 8/8.
